newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Aug 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Aug 14.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories Thursday:
* Visa said debit card customers would not be liable for unauthorized charges if they reported a lost or stolen card within two days.
* Retail spending increased in July, while inflation was more subdued than expected.
* Nissan is declaring vistory for its quirky brand image campaign in the U.S.
* A new fight has broken out among companies developing DVD technology.
* D.H. Blair paid a hefty fine for overcharging customers during the first few days of trading in some new issues.
* The Dow Jones Industrials closed Wednesday down 32.52 at 7928.32.
* Bonds rose as inflation fears eased.
* Federated Department Stores, Dillard's and CompUSA all either met or beat quarterly earnings expectations.
* Fleet Financial is seen close to buying Columbia Management for between $500 million and $600 million.

* First Capital Strategists and its four partners were ordered by regulators to return $2.6 million to colleges that lost more than $137 million on unthorized investments by a former trader who worked for the company's Common Fund.
* Chrysler said it is cutting prices on its 1998 models 0.6 percent.
* Publishers can reproduce articles by freelance writers in some electronic media without the writers' permission, a federal judge ruled.
* Disney's ABC unit plans to lay off nearly 200 employees as it prepares to submit its budget to Disney, executives said.
* Ontario is shutting down seven of its 19 operating nuclear reactors.
* Talks in the United Parcel Service-Teamsters union strike are slated to resume Thursday.
* Representatives of cigarette companies and state attornies met to renegotiate parts of the tobacco settlement.
